subject: Private offer request for EduTech pilot — discount + rev-share ask
messages:
From: Amina Hassan <amina@edutech.edu>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edutech.edu>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Private offer for academic pilot — request for deep edu discount + marketplace carve-out

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the call this morning. EduTech Labs is running a research pilot (12 months) across 5 campuses and we'd like to procure Redwood through the AWS Marketplace private offer route. A couple of asks to see if you can accommodate:

- We need an education program discount (target 50% off list) given academic pricing constraints.
- Payment terms: net-60 for the pilot.
- Marketplace rev-share: because our institution facilitates marketplace procurement and has an existing reseller arrangement, we're asking Redwood to accept a 5% rev-share to the partner for this private offer (rather than the standard 15%).

We're on a timeline to get procurement approval and a PO in hand by the end of November. I've attached a short RFP and the estimated seat counts. Can you confirm whether a private offer + rev-share carve-out is possible and what approvals are required?

Appreciate it —
Amina Hassan
Director, Procurement
EduTech Labs
attachment: EduTech_RFP.pdf (1 page)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Amina Hassan <amina@edutech.edu>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer for academic pilot — request for deep edu discount + marketplace carve-out

Hi Amina —

Thanks for the details and the RFP. Quick confirmation: we can run this via an AWS private offer but the rev-share and payment-term asks are non-standard and will require Deal Desk + Finance + Partnerships alignment. I'm looping in Karhtik (Deal Desk) and Marissa (Partnerships/Finance) to scope the commercial impact and next steps.

A few facts from our side to speed the review:
- Typical marketplace rev-share is 15% for private offers; marketing co-funding or onboarding credits can be used to offset sticker price if we need to move the rev-share.
- For education programs we have precedent for larger discounts on multi-campus pilots but usually paired with a minimum commitment or marketing/PR joint outcomes.
- AWS requires the private offer to be configured by us + the purchaser; rev-share percentages are part of the offer metadata and need explicit approval.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karhtik — can you run an initial impact calc (ARR, expected first-year revenue, margin delta) and advise tolerable rev-share range?
2) Marissa/Laura — flag if net-60 is acceptable for this customer profile; if not, propose alternatives (e.g., net-30 with ledgered credit).
3) Amina — can you confirm final expected ARR for year 1 (annualized) and whether EduTech will provide co-marketing (case study/pilot PR)?

Deal ID for tracking: RDW-2025-4801.

I'll hold on submitting the private offer until we have approvals.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer for academic pilot — request for deep edu discount + marketplace carve-out

Logan / team,

Thanks for looping me in. I pulled the preliminary numbers based on the RFP assumptions (5 campuses, 100 seats each, estimated avg usage). Attachments: pricing_workbook.xlsx, revshare_model_v1.csv.

Key ask summary from our side:
- A 50% list discount plus a 5% marketplace rev-share has a material margin impact (~40% reduction on first-year gross margin).
- If we keep marketplace rev-share at 15% (standard) and provide a blended education discount at 30% with a 12-month pilot commitment, the net revenue delta is more manageable.
- If the customer needs the rev-share to be 5% due to their procurement rules, a potential compromise is: 8% rev-share for first 12 months + a one-time marketing credit of $40k (to offset partner/marketplace fees), with strict measurement of pilot outcomes.

Questions for the customer to confirm before escalation:
- Confirm first-year committed spend (po or commitment letter).
- Confirm willingness to co-fund a case study and to participate in a webinar.

Assuming EduTech confirms ARR >= $750k and commits to co-marketing, I recommend escalating for an executive exception to allow an 8% rev-share for year one with the marketing credit and net-60 payment. If ARR < $750k, we should deny the 5% request and offer standard rev-share + deeper upfront discount paired with a PO and net-30.

I'll prepare a short exec summary for sign-off if we get the customer confirmations.

- Karthik
Deal Desk Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 08:26:00 -0800
Subject: Exec approval request: EduTech RDW-2025-4801 — rev-share exception proposal

Evelyn —

Looping you in for an expedited exec approval. Deal summary (short):
- Account: EduTech Labs (higher-ed consortium)
- Ask: 50% education discount; net-60 payment; marketplace rev-share at 5% for partner carve-out
- Proposed compromise: 30% education discount; 8% rev-share for initial 12-month pilot; $40k marketing/integration credit; require co-marketing deliverables + PO for full pilot amount
- Estimated first-year ARR: $820,000 (per pricing_workbook.xlsx)
- Estimated first-year net revenue to Redwood under proposed compromise: ~$592k after rev-share and credits (see revshare_model_v1.csv)
- Key risks: extended payment terms (net-60) and precedent-setting for edu discounts via marketplace.

Recommendation: approve one-time exception to grant 8% rev-share for 12 months with the stated marketing credit and require contract clause that prevents auto-reduction of price for subsequent renewals. Also require Legal to attach a DPA addendum for academic data use.

If approved, next admin steps:
1) Finance to confirm AR/collection guardrails for net-60 (Laura).
2) Partnerships to own marketing credit execution (Marissa).
3) Sales to coordinate with AWS to build private offer and set the rev-share metadata.
4) Legal to draft DPA addendum and the private offer terms.

Please reply with ok / need more info. This is time-sensitive — procurement needs a signed offer by 11/25 to meet their internal review cycle.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Partnerships & Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
attachment: pricing_workbook.xlsx
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 Nov 2025 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exec approval request: EduTech RDW-2025-4801 — rev-share exception proposal

Marissa / team —

Ok to approve the one-time exception with the conditions you listed. To be explicit:
- Approve 8% marketplace rev-share for the first 12 months only.
- Approve 30% education discount vs list.
- Approve $40k marketing/integration credit, payable after co-marketing deliverables are met.
- Approve net-60 only if legal-approved PO with a late-fee clause and Finance confirms AR monitoring cadence.
- Require Legal to add the DPA addendum and ensure no renewal auto-escalation to lower pricing without exec sign-off.

Logan — proceed to capture customer confirmation on ARR and co-marketing. Karhtik / Marissa / Laura: please get the private offer configured with these metadata values and loop AWS Marketplace ops (aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com) — confirm they can model the 8% rev-share on their side.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Revenue & Partnerships | Redwood Inference
